newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks correct, construction leads market lower.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks correct, construction leads market lower.

text.p: Greek shares traded in negative territory on Tuesday giving up some of their recent gains to close 0.72 percent lower. Construction shares and banks led the market lower with industrials also trading weaker.
But market watchers saw a stronger market after the 1997 budget comes out expecting the benchmark index to be trading at higher levels in December.

"The market paused its two-day advance for a correction today. But I expect a more dynamic market in December. Along with a seasonality factor, if the 1997 budget meets market expectations it will also spark a runup to around 1000-1100 points by late December-January," said analyst Nick Galousis at Kappa Securities.
"If the government finally chooses to tax interest earned on state debt paper, equities will benefit," he said.

Financial market focus has turned to government plans to tax interest earned on T-bills, derivatives such as swaps, options and FRAs and revamp the tax status of mutual funds as the market awaits the 1997 budget.
The finance ministry has cut the marker 12-month T-bill by 40 basis points, down to 12.30 percent. The issue came to market last Thursday and sold very well.
National Bank of Greece trimmed its savings deposit rate by 25 basis points down to 11.25 percent effective November 4.
The Athens general share index closed down 0.72 percent or 6.78 points lower and trading volume slipped to 6.2 billion drachmas.
